subject: SSE streaming: p99 tail spike during load test – mitigation plan and customer update
messages:
From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@fablecommerce.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-15T09:10:22-08:00
Subject: [URGENT] High p99 tail on SSE chat during load test

Hi Naomi,

We just finished a Black Friday load simulation from 08:45–09:00 PT and saw sustained p99 latencies on the streaming chat SSE endpoint up to ~6.8s for token chunks and a corresponding bump in 500/502 error rates. This is affecting our livechat widgets in the staging region and we’re seeing user sessions time out.

Quick details:
- Region: us-west-2
- Client library: fable-js@2.1.0 (SSE mode)
- Example timestamps (UTC): 2026-12-15T16:50:12Z, 2026-12-15T16:50:34Z, 2026-12-15T16:51:05Z
- Error pattern: spikes correlate with long-history contexts (>6k tokens) and bursts of concurrent sessions (~1.6k/s).

We’re attaching a small diagnostic packet and a screenshot of the client-side timeouts. Can you triage and advise on immediate mitigations? If you have a recommended short-term fallback (non-streaming or model downgrade), we can flip it on while you investigate. This is blocking our internal acceptance test for our holiday roll-out.

Thanks,
Elena Ortiz
Platform Lead, Fable Commerce

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-12-15T09:23:41-08:00
Subject: Fwd: [URGENT] High p99 tail on SSE chat during load test — need triage and short-term mitigations

Team — forwarding Fable’s report (attached). They’re seeing p99 ~6–7s and increased 5xx during a simulated peak. This looks like the same class of tail problems we saw in November but at higher concurrency.

Immediate asks:
1) Rishi / SRE: please run the SSE gateway and runtime traces for the 16:50:00Z window and confirm whether queuing or kernel slow-paths are dominating. Prioritize KV cache miss rates per tenancy.
2) Aditya: if we need to flip a runtime soft-fallback (chunked responses or non-streaming path) for the tenant, we need a quick toggle and a rollback plan.
3) Marcus / Ops: prep the soft-rate-limit runbook and estimated timeline to deploy across frontends; we may also need to instantly scale SSE frontends.
4) Laura: draft a short customer update (concise, action-oriented).

Attachments: fable_diagnostics_20261215.json, sse_tail_snapshot_0912.png

I’m looping in the on-call folks — this may need exec visibility if it affects their holiday rollout.

— Naomi
Senior Customer Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-15T09:38:10-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: [URGENT] High p99 tail on SSE chat during load test — quick triage

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observed: SSE gateway queuing spike at 16:49:58Z; worker backlog increased from 150 -> 860 queued requests in ~20s.
- Runtime: a measurable jump in KV cache miss rate for tenant Fable (~78% miss) — suggests new prompt patterns evicting cached prefixes.
- Model path: several requests routed to the slow kernel path because sequence windows exceeded optimized chunking (avg seq length ~5.8k tokens).

Immediate mitigation recommendations (minutes):
1) Scale SSE frontends by +40% (auto-scale warm pools) — should reduce queueing and p99 by ~30–45%. (action: Aditya)
2) Enable per-tenant soft-rate-limit (drop to 80% of baseline concurrent streams) for Fable for 15 minutes while we stabilize. This is reversible and cheap to apply. (action: Marcus)
3) Route their heaviest sessions to non-streaming chunked responses for sessions with context >4k tokens — reduces kernel slow path hits. (action: Runtime toggle, Aditya/Rishi)
4) If they accept, switch to a faster, slightly smaller quantized variant (rdw-small-q4f) for the tenant for the test window — improves throughput at minor quality delta. (needs CS + billing opt-in)

I’m attaching a short log snippet and a link to the trace we started. I’ll keep digging into cache eviction patterns; may need a hot-prefix caching fix if this recurs.

[Attachment: rishi_sse_traces_snippet.log]

— Rishi
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-15T10:02:55-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: [URGENT] High p99 tail on SSE chat during load test — ops steps

Operational checklist (I can execute now):
- Enable soft-rate-limit for tenant Fable: estimated 5–10 minutes to push + validate. See runbook: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/sse-soft-rate-limit (attached copy).
- Spin one extra frontend pool in us-west-2 and increase worker concurrency: ~7 minutes for warm-up. Note: transient CPU/GPU cost increase while scaled.
- Coordinate with Billing (cc: finance) if we enable rdw-small-q4f route — will increase inference units for the short window; I’ll send cost delta once we decide.

Risks: if we only throttle without routing to a faster model, some sessions may still time out because of kernel slow-path cost. Recommend combined approach: scale + throttle + model-downgrade as needed.

I’ll stage the runbook actions and post the “done” timestamp in this thread.

[Attachment: runbook_enable_soft_rate_limit.txt]

— Marcus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-15T11:15:03-08:00
Subject: Draft: Customer update to Fable (please review)

Naomi — draft below for Elena. Keep it short and prescriptive.

Subject: Update: Mitigations in place for SSE latency during load test

Hi Elena,

Thanks for the diagnostic — we’ve taken the following immediate actions:
- Scaled SSE frontends in us-west-2 and increased worker concurrency.
- Enabled a temporary soft-rate-limit for Fable to reduce concurrent streaming pressure.
- For heavy sessions (context >4k tokens) we’ve routed to a non-streaming chunked response path to avoid kernel slow-paths.

Estimated impact: we expect p99 to fall by ~30–50% within the next 10–20 minutes. We’re monitoring in real time and will follow up with a short postmortem after the window.

If you prefer, we can also switch the tenant to rdw-small-q4f for the remainder of the test window to further reduce tail latency (minor quality trade-off). Please confirm if you’d like us to flip that.

— Laura
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@fablecommerce.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-15T16:42:05-08:00
Subject: RE: [URGENT] High p99 tail on SSE chat during load test — immediate actions taken

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the quick diagnostic. We implemented the following mitigations and are actively monitoring:
- Scaled SSE frontends in us-west-2 (+40% warm pool).
- Enabled a tenant-level soft-rate-limit for Fable for a 15-minute stabilization window.
- Routed sessions with context >4k tokens to the non-streaming chunked path to avoid the kernel slow path.
- Standby option: we can switch Fable to rdw-small-q4f for the test window if you’d like lower tail latency (minor quality change).

Current status (16:42 PT): p99 has dropped from ~6.8s to ~3.7s in the most recent 10-minute window; error rates have decreased but we’re continuing to watch for re-surge.

Next steps:
- We’ll hold the soft-rate-limit for 15 minutes and then gradually relax while monitoring.
- Postmortem with traces and recommendations within 48 hours.
- If you want an immediate further improvement, reply here and we’ll flip rdw-small-q4f for the active test window.

Apologies for the disruption during your rollout; we’ll prioritize the postmortem and long-term fixes (hot-prefix caching, kernel-path optimizations) so this does not recur.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Customer Engineer, Redwood Inference
